title: Chain rule for conditional mutual information
statement:
Let $X$, $Y$, $Z$, and $W$ be measurable functions on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$, where $\mu$ is either the zero measure or a probability measure, each taking values in a countable measurable space and attaining only finitely many values. Write $I(X ; Y \mid Z)$ for the conditional mutual information between $X$ and $Y$ given $Z$. Then the conditional mutual information between $X$ and the pair $(Y, W)$ given $Z$ satisfies
\[
  I\bigl(X ; (Y, W) \mid Z\bigr) \;=\; I(X ; Y \mid Z) \;+\; I\bigl(X ; W \mid (Y, Z)\bigr).
\]
hypotheses_covered: each valued in a countable measurable space (with measurable singletons)
each of X, Y, W, Z has finite range
replaced:
For measurable $X$, $Y$, $W$, $Z$ with finite ranges under a zero-or-probability measure,
\[
  I[X : (Y, W) \mid Z;\mu]
  \;=\; I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] \;+\; I[X : W \mid (Y, Z);\mu].
\]
